# Todd Paresis

**Authors:** James Mastriana, Jeffrey L. Pay, Orlando De Jesus, Roger S. Taylor

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Todd paresis is a syndrome associated with weakness or paralysis of part or all of the body as soon as the ictal discharge (seizure) has ended. It most commonly affects one limb or one-half of the body but can have a wide range of presentations. Todd paresis is also known as Todd paralysis or Todd palsy. The original concept of motor paresis is now extended to fields including language, oculomotor function, somatosensory, consciousness, and visual field. This condition was initially described by Irish physiologist and physician Robert Bentley Todd in 1849 but has been further defined, researched, and explained by many others over the years. Despite this being a common phenomenon for neurologists, relatively little research has been conducted on the condition.
